Hey team —

Attached a concise tech runbook and sample snippets (sdk-samples-v2.zip). Key points / recommended defaults below so AppLink can start implementing immediately:

1) SDK setup- Node: npm install @redwood/inference@^2.0; init with REDWOOD_API_KEY in env; sample snippet below.
- Go: go get github.com/redwood/inference; examples in /go-samples folder.

2) Endpoint recommendation- Use /v1/stream for real-time responses when you need sub-200ms token turn; /v1/generate for batch or deterministic runs. Start with /v1/generate on staging to validate payloads, then flip a canary to /v1/stream for 10% traffic for latency test.

3) Timeouts and retries (client-side)- TCP/connect timeout: 2s- Initial request timeout: 7s per request for generate; 20s for streaming sessions (client should close after 60s idle).- Retry policy for idempotent requests: exponential backoff with full jitter, max attempts = 4.- 429 handling: honor Retry-After when present; fallback to exponential backoff if absent. When you see sustained 429s, route to a lower-cost model (we can configure routing policies) rather than retrying aggressively.

4) Rate limit headers and observability- Redwood returns X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Surface these in your telemetry and create an alert when Remaining < 15% of Limit for a sliding 5m window.

5) KV/prefix caching- Use local TTL cache for repeated prompt prefixes (we recommend caching 2–3slices of hot prefixes per session) to reduce token counts on repeated calls.

6) Canary + cutover checklist (smoke tests)
- Deploy SDK in staging and run 1000 sample requests at expected concurrency. Validate token usage and latency p95.
- Flip 10% traffic to canary endpoint for 1 hour. Monitor 429s, p95 latency, error rate (<0.5%).
- If canary passes, increase to 50% for 30 minutes then full cutover during low-traffic window.

7) Sample Node snippet (from sdk-samples-v2.zip)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, endpoint: 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' });
async function predict(prompt){
  try{
    const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-3.2', prompt, timeout: 7000 });
    return resp.output;
  } catch (err){
    // Exponential backoff retry logic here
    throw err;
  }
}
